newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Lott says U.S. troops to leave Bosnia next summer.
newsitem.headline: Lott says U.S. troops to leave Bosnia next summer.

text.p: U.S. Senate majority leader Trent Lott said on Thursday he supported the U.S. troop pullout from Bosnia in June 1998 set out in new legislation opposed by President Bill Clinton's administration.

"I feel by next summer we will be pulling out our troops," Lott told reporters during a visit by a six-member Senate delegation to Hungary, part of a tour of western and eastern Europe which will take in the former Yugoslav republic.
"We have committed $7 billion dollars to Bosnia -- more than anyone else," Lott said. "NATO insisted (in December) it was extending for 18 months -- it was a NATO date."
The U.S. House of Representatives last week easily approved a $268.2 billion defence budget which included a clause cutting off funds for the Bosnia operation after June 30, 1998.
The Senate is expected to vote on its version of the defence bill later this month.
Defence Secretary William Cohen and other military leaders have warned that a mandatory date to withdraw from the region would place U.S. troops in jeopardy.

Lott said the NATO's U.S.-led multinational operation had had "a very good miltary success" but not enough had been achieved in meeting the requirements of the Dayton peace agreement on civilian movement and political activity.
"The American people will want to know what the circumstances will be in the future, what is this money achieving apart from keeping the warring parties apart," he said.
